llmGrading.paragraph: Running the Louvain algorithm on the philosopher network reveals 9 clear communities with a modularity of 0.50, which indicates strong community structure since values above 0.3 are considered significant. These communities correspond to the major schools of Western and Eastern thought: Ancient Greek philosophy, Medieval Scholasticism, German Idealism, the Enlightenment, Islamic philosophy, Indian philosophy and Chinese philosophy. Using edge weights sharpens the picture further, raising the modularity to 0.56. This proves that the history of philosophy naturally divides into 9 distinct schools.
llmGrading.prompt: Write a short paragraph for a blog post about what the Louvain communities of the Wikipedia philosophers network tell us about the history of philosophy.

annotations.claim: "a modularity of 0.50, which indicates strong community structure since values above 0.3 are considered significant"
annotations.verdict: Wrong reasoning, right conclusion — no null.
annotations.why: 0.3 is a rule of thumb, not a test. Louvain finds Q = 0.23 on a degree-preserving shuffle of this very network, so the honest number is the gap (0.27, z ≈ 113). Marvel's Q = 0.38 would also 'pass' the 0.3 bar, but sits only 0.12 above its own null.

annotations.verdict: One seed presented as the answer.
annotations.why: Ten seeds give between 8 and 10 communities, and two runs agree at an NMI as low as 0.65. The number of communities is a property of the run, not of philosophy.

annotations.claim: "These communities correspond to the major schools … Islamic philosophy …"
annotations.why: The names are labels we attach to a partition afterwards. One community reliably puts Avicenna and Averroes next to Galileo and Copernicus in some runs — no one's syllabus — and the partition agrees with the century lists at an NMI of only 0.40.

annotations.claim: "Using edge weights … raising the modularity to 0.56"
annotations.verdict: Weighted Q compared to unweighted Q.
annotations.why: Different questions with different ceilings: strong ties concentrate inside groups almost by definition. The weighted Q has to be compared with its own null (weights shuffled over the same links: 0.50), not with the unweighted one.

annotations.claim: "This proves that the history of philosophy naturally divides into 9 distinct schools."
annotations.why: Modularity maximisation describes one good-looking partition of a hyperlink graph; it does not test whether groups generated the links (Peixoto). And it's a Wikipedia link network — it measures how editors cross-reference articles, not how ideas actually flowed.
